title: VRUN CTW (NES demake of Corrupt The World, NESFab, mapper 30)
description: The NES demake of the HTML5 game CTW, written in NESFab for mapper 30 (UNROM-512: 512 KB PRG, CHR-RAM, self-flashing SST39SF040 saves). The shared audio engine (engine/audio, with the C# MIDI converter) runs inside every build.

toolchain: Mesen 2.1.1 shipped in tools/mesen (the project's regression suite oracle; BrokenDev uses BrokenNes instead)

steps.name: build-game
steps.note: prebuild.sh runs the C# music converter (dotnet), the CTW map bake (node) and the CHR bake (python); the build ends with 'PASS - ROM matches the target cartridge spec.'

run.note: Title: NEW GAME / CONTINUE / OPTIONS. Start begins. In game, Start pauses and Select then saves (16 bytes to flash sector 118).

compare.why: scripted input reached the game: the same frame number looks different with and without input

oracle.why: Mesen 2.1.1 (the baseline the VRUN accuracy campaign used) and BrokenNes FIX cores run the same ROM with the same pad script; per frame the picture (palette indices), nametables, OAM, palette, CHR, PPU control and every APU register must agree. Uses the user's Mesen tracer, kept in BrokenDev/tools/vrun/mesen/state_trace.lua (BROKENDEV_TRACE_LUA names another).

compat.what: VRUN on other NES emulators (brokendev.ps1 compat vrun-nes): the game's own state read through its .mlb symbols every frame, pictures at the checkpoints. Emulators boot a few frames apart, so states are compared with a frame tolerance. The map seed rotates every title frame (map_slot), so the first room may differ between emulators: current_room is recorded, never compared.

scenarios.what: power-on, the title, Start, then verify's play script

checks.what: boots to the title (app_state APP_TITLE = 0 before Start)
the title runs (the NMI counter ticks)
a first boot has no save (save_exists 0)
the title looks like BrokenNes' title (structure, palette aside)
the first room finishes loading (room_load_phase reaches its last phase, 9)
the scripted play stays in the game (no death, no return to the title)
the game keeps running to the end (the NMI counter keeps ticking)
gameplay is drawn at the end

scenarios.what: Start, pause (Start), Select = save and quit: 16 bytes to the mapper-30 flash (sector 118)

checks.what: save and quit returns to the title
the title cursor lands on CONTINUE (title_cursor 1)

scenarios.what: a fresh boot of the same emulator, its battery save from 'save' in place

checks.what: a fresh boot finds the save (save_exists 1: CONTINUE is offered)
BrokenDev hardware checks (docs/projects/brokendev-debugging-plan.md, D4): every verify scenario runs again with the checks on; a finding not accepted here fails verify. Each acceptance says why.

accepted.reason: known: VRUN lags while it boots (frames 3-13: ppu_upload_pbz unpacks the title) and while a room loads (2 frames after Start, 5 at a room change: decompress_room, close_all_doors, spawn_hazards_from_markers); the lagFrames budget gates normal play

budgets.what: Over a limit fails verify, near it (90%) warns; the report compares with the previous build (out/<id>/budget-history.json). romBankFree is an estimate (padding runs of 64 or more equal $00 / $FF bytes).

lagFrames.what: after the first room has loaded; 5 on 2026-10-24 (one room change, frames 608-612)

busyPercent.what: the busiest frame that made it: 58.5% on 2026-10-24

memoryFree.what: RAM never read in the scenarios: 825 bytes on 2026-10-24

stackFree.what: 217 bytes between the deepest stack and the data below it on 2026-10-24

romBankFree.what: the fixed bank 31 (the code every bank calls): 1548 bytes of padding runs on 2026-10-24

knownIssues: start_at_option_check fails in the project's own regression suite (the START AT spawn bug, blocked by the ROM budget); 67 of 68 checks pass.
The ROM is at its ceiling: fixed bank 31 has no slack and each extra 'mode main()' branch costs about 1200 IR nodes.
NESFab miscompiles are real (three confirmed in the disassembly). When a harmless edit breaks something, disassemble before theorising.

The build is not byte-reproducible: two builds of the same source gave different ROMs (sha256 584a91bc... and 3cfce10c..., measured by BrokenDev on 2026-10-16) with the same picture at the end of both UAT cases (frames 900 and 2400). Compare behaviour (BrokenDev verify, UAT), not file hashes.

On BrokenNes the NES runs 48.5 CPU cycles per frame more than hardware unless 'NTSC-accurate frame timing' is on (the app default is off, as an accuracy-for-speed trade). The play-ntsc scenario runs the same input with it on.

movies.why: verify's play script as a movie (Start, then running and jumping through the first rooms, D5's promoted-movie proof on a real game): on the build it was recorded on every keyframe must match; on a new build the keyframes are information and these expectations decide

memory.what: still in the game at the end (APP_GAME), no return to the title
